raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem
Since #45231, `LoRAMemoryPool._has_moe_module` checks each `FusedMoE` against `should_apply_lora(name)`. The pool is built after `init_lora_modules()` wraps the experts, so the `FusedMoE` is named `<name>.base_layer`, and patterns anchored at `mlp.experts` (gpt-oss, MiMo-V2) reject it. These models then get dense 3D buffers:
- gpt-oss MoE LoRA fails CUDA graph capture with `NotImplementedError: virtual-expert MoE LoRA does not support padded Marlin outputs`
- the MiMo-V2 Tinker LoRA test raises `IndexError: tuple index out of range` at `lora_b_list[0].shape[3]` in `virtual_experts.py`

This broke the miles nightly gpt-oss and MiMo LoRA tests (https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/40528466754).

## Fix
Match `should_apply_lora` against the name without `.base_layer`. Experts a model keeps out of LoRA, such as DeepSeek-V4's routed experts, are never wrapped, so they stay excluded.

## Tests
- New regression test `TestHasMoeModuleAfterWrapping` in `test_mem_pool_ep_unit.py`: fails before the fix, passes after. All 61 tests in the file pass.
- End to end on 2x H200, miles `tests/e2e/megatron/model_scripts/test_gpt_oss_20b_moe_lora_ci.py`: fails at sglang `b8d46f2`, passes at `8237a5b` (before #45231) and with this fix.
- Miles CI with this PR pinned (`ci-sglang-pr: #46894` on https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/4484), both tests that failed in the nightly now pass:
  - `test_gpt_oss_20b_moe_lora_ci.py`: PASS in 839s, both the per-expert and the shared-outer + virtual-experts configs (https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/40602473473)
  - `tests/e2e/lora/test_tinker_mimo_v2_6_4layer.py`: PASS in 233s (https://github.com/radixark/miles/actions/runs/40602452095)

files.patch:
@@ -376,7 +376,11 @@ def _has_moe_module(base_model: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:
         should_apply_lora = getattr(base_model, "should_apply_lora", None)
         return any(
             isinstance(module, FusedMoE)
-            and (should_apply_lora is None or should_apply_lora(name))
+            # init_lora_modules() runs first, so wrapped experts sit at `<name>.base_layer`
+            and (
+                should_apply_lora is None
+                or should_apply_lora(name.removesuffix(".base_layer"))
+            )
             for name, module in base_model.named_modules()
         )

@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@
 
 import ast
 import itertools
+import re
 import types
 import unittest
 import unittest.mock as mock
@@ -1991,5 +1992,37 @@ def test_an_all_moe_model_gets_only_expert_buffers(self):
         self.assertEqual(sorted(pool.B_buffer), ["down_proj_moe", "gate_up_proj_moe"])
 
 
+@mock.patch.dict(
+    "sys.modules", {"sglang.srt.layers.moe.fused_moe_triton.layer": _FUSED_MOE_STUB}
+)
+class TestHasMoeModuleAfterWrapping(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Experts already wrapped for LoRA must still get per-expert buffers when the
+    model's `should_apply_lora` pattern names `mlp.experts` (gpt-oss, MiMo-V2)."""
+
+    class _Wrapper(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self, base_layer):
+            super().__init__()
+            self.base_layer = base_layer
+
+    class _Model(torch.nn.Module):
+        def __init__(self, experts, lora_pattern):
+            super().__init__()
+            self.model = torch.nn.Module()
+            self.model.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList([torch.nn.Module()])
+            self.model.layers[0].mlp = torch.nn.Module()
+            self.model.layers[0].mlp.experts = experts
+            self.should_apply_lora = lambda name: bool(lora_pattern.match(name))
+
+    PATTERN = re.compile(r"^model\.layers\.\d+\.mlp\.experts$")
+
+    def test_wrapped_experts_count_as_moe(self):
+        model = self._Model(self._Wrapper(_FakeFusedMoE()), self.PATTERN)
+        self.assertTrue(LoRAMemoryPool._has_moe_module(model))
+
+    def test_experts_the_model_excludes_stay_out(self):
+        model = self._Model(_FakeFusedMoE(), re.compile(r"^model\.embed_tokens$"))
+        self.assertFalse(LoRAMemoryPool._has_moe_module(model))
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
